answers.how: Measured apparent length and 2D position of the astronaut across frames around t=0.5s, reconstructed 3D coordinates using the 2.2 m height prior and depth at t=1s (23.137 m), and computed the 3D speed.

Computed the 3D velocity at t=1s from the rate of change of apparent size (depth) and transverse pixel position scaled by the 2.2 m height prior at Z=23.137 m.
Derived from the second derivative of the reconstructed 3D position of the astronaut at t=1s.
Calculated 3D speed at t=2s from the reconstructed 3D positions using inverse-distance scaling of the astronaut's apparent pixel length.
Derived from the second derivative of the reconstructed 3D trajectory at t=2s.
Calculated 3D speed at t=3s from the rate of change of reconstructed 3D coordinates around frame 72.
Derived from the second derivative of the reconstructed 3D trajectory at t=3s.
